findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count = 100 and limit = 50 it returns 3, but only 2 pages exist. The 'next' action then sets offset to 100 and loads an empty page, and showingLast stays false on page 2. The same applies to any exact multiple. The page count should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

findings.title: 'next' can set offset to user_count, which produces an empty page
findings.body: offset is computed as Math.min(offset + limit, user_count). Offsets should step by whole pages. Combined with the totalPages off-by-one, paging forward can land on an offset equal to user_count, and findMembers then requests an empty page. Offsets should advance by limit and be bounded by the last page start, not by user_count.

findings.title: Offset clamp to user_count yields an empty page after removing the last member on a page
findings.body: findMembers clamps offset to user_count. If a page is at offset 50 with 51 users and one member is removed, user_count becomes 50. The clamp then keeps offset at 50, so the reloaded page is empty even though page 1 has members. The offset should be moved back to the start of the last existing page, not left at user_count.

findings.title: findMembers now returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name
findings.body: The early return was changed from Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to a bare return. Callers that chain .then on the result, which is a common pattern in this codebase, will throw a TypeError for unnamed groups. Returning a resolved promise keeps the contract.

findings.title: Client-controlled limit has no upper bound and no validation
findings.body: limit comes straight from params as (params[:limit] || 50).to_i. A caller can request an arbitrarily large page of members, which defeats pagination and allows bulk enumeration of group membership in one request for any visible group. Negative values also reach SQL LIMIT and raise an error. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum and a minimum of 1, and offset should be clamped to be non-negative.

findings.title: Members endpoint response shape changed for all groups
findings.body: The members action now returns {members:, meta:} instead of a bare serialized array for every group, including automatic groups that previously returned a plain array. Any other client of /groups/:name/members, not just the updated admin and group templates, will break. This is an API change that is not called out.

findings.title: automatic flag is looked up on the member, so the remove link shows for automatic groups
findings.body: Inside an itemView the context is the individual member (a User), not the group. {{#unless automatic}} therefore checks member.automatic, which is undefined, so the remove link is always rendered. Clicking it on an automatic group yields a 422 from the server. The parent group's automatic flag needs to be passed into the item view or the controller.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT while the route is DELETE
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route is defined as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member". The spec does not exercise the real HTTP verb and could pass for the wrong reason. It should use :delete.

findings.title: No specs for the new paginated members endpoint or for the non-admin path
findings.body: The PR rewrites GroupsController#members to add pagination, limit/offset handling, and a meta payload, but no spec covers it. It also removes the 'cannot patch automatic groups' and incremental-membership tests without replacement for the public members endpoint. Pagination edge cases (limit bounds, offset past end, total count) are untested.

findings.title: Stale selector references the removed group-users id
findings.body: The rule `input#group-users { width: 600px; }` still targets the id that the template no longer uses (it now uses user-selector). The rule is dead and the intended width for the member input is no longer applied.
